Unfortunately, it feels like the service at Woodseats Medical Centre is getting worse.

I submitted a request for a repeat prescription today and heard nothing back. I waited around expecting some kind of confirmation or phone call, but by 2pm I had to call the practice myself to find out what was going on. After ringing for about 10 minutes with no hold music or queue system, someone finally answered and told me the medication had already been prescribed and sent to the chemist.

The problem is I received absolutely no notification or message to say this had happened. No text, no email, nothing. This kind of communication breakdown is not just frustrating, it’s potentially dangerous. Elderly or vulnerable patients could easily be left waiting for days thinking their medication hasn't been sorted, when in fact it's sitting at the pharmacy.

This system clearly isn’t working and needs serious improvement. At the very least, patients should be informed when their prescriptions are ready. Communication is essential in healthcare, and right now, it’s badly lacking.

When I asked why no notification was sent, the response I received was that the practice “doesn’t have the manpower” to inform patients. Frankly, this is a poor excuse. Communication is an essential part of healthcare, not an optional extra. If the current system relies on patients chasing up their own prescriptions, then it’s simply not fit for purpose.
